messages.subject: Re: traditional parameterization/plotting for multi-dimensional models
parts:
They can, but not practically. The difficulty parameters reflect points of inflection in the probability functions, which for multidimensional models would be infinitely divisible vectors of difficulties relating to P(theta, a1, a2, d1) = .5. This is generally why the slope intercept version is preferred as they scale the probability functions in more reasonably anchored locations. HTH.

Phil

Hello,

I have a one- two-  three-dimensional model and a joint-model, and I want to compare (if different) and describe the difficulty parameters of these models. My question is: is it possible to obtain traditional parameterization for these models? Something similar to the IRT = T command for the summary function for uni-dimensional models. There are no cross-loadings in these models, so in my head, this would seem like a reasonable thing to do? However, I can't find any information on it here or in the package description. 

Thanks in advance,
Sverre Ofstad
